column1: # tests/runtime-budgets.tsv — per-file wall-clock ceilings (change 0227).
# Format: <repo-relative test path><TAB><max seconds><TAB><parallel|serial>
# WHY: the suite was 629s because four files grew to 66% of it. A one-time split decays;
# this table is the discipline made durable. Seeded from the measured post-shard run,
# rounded up to the next multiple of 5 plus a 5s margin (min 10s).
# A new tests/test_*.sh with NO row here fails tests/test_runtime_budgets.sh. That is
# deliberate: adding a test file is a conscious placement decision. Read tests/README.md
# before adding one — the usual right answer is to EXTEND an existing shard.
# NO row may exceed 60 seconds — with ONE documented exemption: tests/test_go_race.sh, the
# serial-isolated whole-module race gate, carries a 300s row under its own sub-ceiling in
# tests/test_runtime_budgets.sh (RELIEF COUNTER A; a TEMPORARY hole owned by follow-up change
# 0333). If any other file outgrows its ceiling, shard it or move the new
# assertions into a shard with room. Raising a number here is not the remedy, and it is not
# a quiet edit either: tests/test_runtime_budgets.sh pins the SUM of every ceiling in this
# table (EXPECTED_TOTAL), so a raise of any size reddens whether or not it breaks the 60s
# ceiling. The total does legitimately move when a new test file brings its own row, or when
# a sharded file's rows are re-cut — re-seed it from a measured serial run and say which.
# tests/test_docket_status.sh was raised 45 -> 50 and then 50 -> 60 by change 0118, which adds two
# sweep runs, three fault-injection runs, and — from review finding 2 — one wedged-shared-worktree
# sweep run to the one file that owns sweep_execute coverage. The first raise's note argued from a
# pre-change reading taken in another session against a post-change reading that came out FASTER,
# which is not an argument; both were re-taken for review finding 6, PAIRED AND INTERLEAVED in one
# session on one machine, each run standalone and serial as
# `/usr/bin/time -p bash tests/test_docket_status.sh` (the base leg is origin/main's copy of the
# file, run from tests/ under a temporary name so it resolves the same REPO root):
#   base (origin/main):  41.59  41.50  41.75  -> worst 41.75
# So the six new fixtures cost about 3.2s of real runtime. That is the honest basis: the file was
# NOT already at parity with its old 45 row, and the raise is driven by added runtime rather than by
# noise. Sizing per this header's rule takes the WORST standalone serial reading recorded for the
# post-change file on this machine, which is 51.36 (the finding-2 readings were 45.17, 46.79, 51.36,
# 50.52, 46.12, 45.14; that ~6s spread is machine load, as the tight interleaved pairs above show):
# next multiple of 5 is 55, plus the 5s margin -> 60. The quiet readings alone would have yielded 50
# (44.92 -> 45, plus 5), so 60 is the conservative pick between the two — a ceiling a loaded machine
# still meets. Sharding was considered and REJECTED HERE: changes 0268 and 0154 are both queued
# against this same file, and re-cutting shards is precisely the edit that cannot rebase cleanly
# past them — the shard belongs to whichever change can take the whole file, not to one adding six
# fixtures to it.
# THIS FILE IS NOW AT THE 60s CEILING. There is no next raise. The next change that adds runtime
# here — 0268 and 0154 are both queued against it — must SHARD the file first; that is now the only
# available move, and it was already the header's stated remedy.
# tests/test_run_tests.sh was raised 20 -> 30 by change 0221, which gates scripts/run-tests.sh on
# the scripts/check-test-source-hygiene.sh preflight. This is the case the header calls a file that
# GOT SLOWER, and the raise is defended by measurement rather than by the feature being new. The
# preflight is per-runner-invocation and this file invokes the runner ~35 times, so it pays the
# preflight ~35 times over. Three standalone serial readings each, one session, one machine, as
# `/usr/bin/time -p bash tests/test_run_tests.sh >/dev/null` (base = origin/main extracted with
# `git archive` into a scratch tree, so it runs its own runner, not this branch's):
#   base (origin/main):        16.16  16.09  16.16  -> worst 16.16
#   branch, sweep unbatched:   27.21  27.24         -> worst 27.24
#   branch, sweep batched:     20.87  20.95  21.03  -> worst 21.03
# The middle row is why this is not simply a raise: rule (a)'s tests-tree sweep forked one awk per
# tests-tree file on EVERY invocation, so the file paid O(#test files x #invocations) and the term
# grew with the suite. Batching the sweep into ONE awk process (verdict-preserving: the checker's
# full output over the live tree and every fixture is byte-identical before and after) gives back
# 6.2s of the 11.1s and, more to the point, makes the remaining cost O(1) awk processes per
# invocation instead of O(#test files). The residual ~4.9s over base is the preflight actually
# running, which is the feature. Sizing per this header's rule from the worst post-change reading,
# 21.03: next multiple of 5 is 25, plus the 5s margin -> 30. Sharding was considered and rejected:
# 21s is nowhere near the 60s ceiling, and the file is one coherent runner-contract suite.
# tests/test_docket_stack.sh is a NEW FILE brought by change 0298 — the header's first legitimate
# case for the total moving. It covers a new subsystem: the stacked-changes library
# (scripts/lib/docket-stack.sh) and, once change 0298's later tasks land, the scripts/stack-base.sh
# CLI over it. It is not an extension of an existing shard because no shard owns stack resolution,
# and the two files it would otherwise have joined are both spent — tests/test_docket_status.sh sits
# at the 60s ceiling and tests/test_board_checks.sh at 55s. Sized per this header's rule from three
# standalone serial readings, one session, one machine, as
# `/usr/bin/time -p bash tests/test_docket_stack.sh >/dev/null`:
# The file drives sourced shell functions over a fixture tree in $TMPDIR with no git and no network,
# so it costs essentially nothing: next multiple of 5 is 5, plus the 5s margin -> 10, which is also
# this table's floor. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 1750 -> 1760 for that one row.
# tests/test_docket_status_stack.sh is a NEW FILE brought by change 0298 — the second legitimate
# mover in this change. It is a SIBLING SHARD of tests/test_docket_status.sh, not an extension of
# it, and the reason is written three notes above in this very header: that file sits AT the 60s
# ceiling and the header states there is no next raise for it. Its new legs — the sweep flipping a
# child whose PR merged into its stack parent's branch to `stacked-merged`, and the discriminating
# case of a stacked child merged into the integration branch, which still closes out to `done` —
# therefore land in their own file. Sized per this header's rule from three standalone serial
# readings, one session, one machine, as
# `/usr/bin/time -p bash tests/test_docket_status_stack.sh >/dev/null`:
# One fixture repo, one stubbed gh, four mocked close-out scripts and no network: next multiple of 5
# is 5, plus the 5s margin -> 10, this table's floor. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 1760 -> 1770.
# tests/test_stack_closeout.sh is a NEW FILE brought by change 0298 — the third and last legitimate
# mover in this change. It owns scripts/stack-closeout.sh, the pass that promotes a merged root's
# `stacked-merged` descendants to `done`, plus stack_descendants in the stacked-changes library. Its
# own file rather than an extension: it drives five independent fixture families (happy path,
# idempotency against the metadata branch, a resumed partial run, a malformed-marker refusal, and a
# cyclic graph) through a real bare origin, and neither sibling shard has room — the two files it
# would otherwise have joined sit at the 60s and 55s ceilings. Sized per this header's rule from
# three standalone serial readings, one session, one machine, as
# `/usr/bin/time -p bash tests/test_stack_closeout.sh >/dev/null`:
# The cost is git: one bare origin, two clones and roughly thirty commits and pushes across the five
# families, with every close-out helper mocked and no network beyond the local origin. Next multiple
# of 5 above 5.45 is 10, plus the 5s margin -> 15. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 1770 -> 1785.
# tests/test_board_checks_stack.sh is a NEW FILE brought by change 0298 — the fourth and last
# legitimate mover in this change. It is a SIBLING SHARD of tests/test_board_checks.sh, which sits
# at 55s: it owns the two stacked health checks (`stack-invalid`, `stack-parent-killed`) and the
# separateness pin that keeps them two ids rather than one. The registration guards stay in
# tests/test_board_checks.sh — they are derived from board-checks.sh itself and belong with the rest
# of the registry — so this file carries only the behavioral legs. Sized per this header's rule from
# three standalone serial readings, one session, one machine, as
# `/usr/bin/time -p bash tests/test_board_checks_stack.sh >/dev/null`:
# The cost is git: one bare origin, one clone, three branches and one pushed feature branch, then
# two board-checks.sh runs over ten fixtures. Next multiple of 5 is 5, plus the 5s margin -> 10,
# this table's floor. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 1785 -> 1795.
# tests/test_go_toolchain.sh is a NEW FILE brought by change 0304 — the header's first legitimate
# case again, and for a brand-new subsystem in the sense tests/README.md means it: the Go module at
# the repository root. It is the whole-suite Go gate, running gofmt, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`
# and the four-tuple CGO-off cross-build. No existing shard could take it — every other file in this
# table drives Bash scripts, and this one's cost is a Go toolchain compiling the module and the four
# approved target tuples. Sized per this header's rule from standalone serial readings, one session,
# one machine, as `scripts/run-tests.sh -j 1 --timings PATH tests/test_go_toolchain.sh`:
# Note what dominates that number: those readings are COLD-CACHE ones. Next multiple of 5 above 13
# is 15, plus the 5s margin -> 20, leaving 8s of margin over the 12s readings. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves
# 1795 -> 1815. Change 0304's review then pinned GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE to a stable per-checkout
# location (the file's own CACHES header has the rationale), so only the first run after a fresh
# clone is cold: re-measured at 12s cold and 2s warm, same command. The ceiling STAYS AT 20 — this
# header sizes from the worst standalone serial reading, and a cold cache is still reachable on any
# fresh clone or CI image. The extra margin is headroom, not slack to reclaim.
# tests/test_go_race.sh is the whole-module data-race gate (change 0308), sharded four ways by
# changes 0309/0313/0314 to fit the parallel phase's 60s ceiling, and COLLAPSED back to a single
# `go test -race ./...` run by change 0332 — which also moved it to the SERIAL lane. The shards
# existed to fit the parallel phase, and the parallel phase is what 0332 removed this gate from:
# `go test -race` spawns GOMAXPROCS-wide race workers that oversubscribed the cores the other
# parallel jobs needed, making the whole suite load-dependent (change 0329's build-gate halt). In
# the serial lane the four shard invocations ran sequentially and summed to ~299s, while one
# `./...` invocation measures ~206s standalone serial because go test overlaps packages
# internally — the collapse is strictly faster AND retires the four-shard completeness guard.
# The ~206s is dominated by internal/app (~200s under -race, ~190s uninstrumented — a ~1.05x
# multiplier: the cost is the package's own integration suite, one Go package, unshardable by
# `go list`). The row is 300, ABOVE the 60s hard ceiling: this table's ONE documented exemption,
# path-keyed and sub-ceilinged at RELIEF COUNTER A in tests/test_runtime_budgets.sh, serial-bound
# by that file's serial-identity assert, TEMPORARY, and owned by follow-up change 0333 (partition
# internal/app). 300 rather than the sizing rule's 215 (206 -> 210 + 5) is deliberate headroom
# for a ~3.5-minute gate whose reading moves with machine load; when 0333 lands, the row and the
# exemption shrink with it. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 2140 -> 2265: -25 -45 -45 for the deleted shard
# rows, +240 for the 60 -> 300 re-cut.
# tests/test_go_toolchain.sh 20 -> 45 (change 0309): a file that GOT SLOWER, defended by measurement.
# Its `go test ./...` now compiles and runs change 0309's internal/repository/transaction package,
# whose real-git acceptance tests add real uninstrumented cost to the whole-suite Go gate. No cost was
# avoidable to remove first: the package's tests ARE the change's acceptance proof. Re-measured
# standalone serial, one machine, as `scripts/run-tests.sh -j 1 --timings PATH tests/test_go_toolchain.sh`:
# Next multiple of 5 above 39 is 40, plus the 5s margin -> 45, still well under the 60s ceiling.
# tests/test_asset_bundle_drift.sh is a NEW FILE brought by change 0311 — the header's new-test-file
# case again, for a subsystem this table has no shard for: the generated, committed embedded
# asset bundle (internal/assets/embedded) and its comparator, `cmd/genassets -check`. It is NOT an
# extension of tests/test_go_toolchain.sh, the only other Go-touching file here: that file is the
# whole-suite Go gate and its `go test ./...` verdict is exactly the cacheable one that CANNOT see
# this drift, since editing skills/ does not change internal/assets' package inputs. Sized per this
# header's rule from three standalone serial readings, one session, one machine, as
# `/usr/bin/time -p bash tests/test_asset_bundle_drift.sh >/dev/null`:
# Those are warm-cache readings, and unlike tests/test_go_toolchain.sh the cold case is cheap here
# and was measured rather than assumed: the file compiles ONE small stdlib-only command
# (cmd/genassets and internal/assets pull no module requirements), so a run with GOMODCACHE and
# GOCACHE both pointed at empty scratch directories costs 2.24s — which also makes the file offline
# after a fresh clone. Its other work is a `cp -R` of four small authored roots (~520K, 64 files)
# plus the generated tree, and three comparator runs over them. Next multiple of 5 above 2.24 is 5,
# plus the 5s margin -> 10, this table's floor. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 1815 -> 1825.
# tests/test_sync_agents_runners.sh was SHARDED by change 0324 — the header's re-cut case, not a
# file that got slower. The runner suite sat AT the hard 60s ceiling with no next raise (its row was
# the ceiling itself), and adding the 17th shipped agent (docket-plan-writer) to the runner matrix
# pushed its measured serial cost to ~96s. The table's own remedy for a file over its ceiling is a
# shard, never a bigger number, so the one file was cut along its `# ---` banner seams into three
# siblings — a MOVE with no assertion changed: 308 runtime asserts split 125/98/85, none lost.
#   tests/test_sync_agents_runners.sh        — runner shims + shim_model/shim_effort config (0079/0269)
#   tests/test_sync_agents_runners_gates.sh  — --worktree slot, required-model, atomic generation
#   tests/test_sync_agents_runners_pins.sh   — resolved model/effort pin injection (0168/0173)
# Sized per this header's rule from three standalone serial readings, one session, one machine, as
# `time bash tests/<shard>.sh`:
#   runners        38.76 38.72 38.78 -> worst 38.78 -> next multiple of 5 is 40, plus 5 -> 45
#   runners_gates  26.78 26.87 26.71 -> worst 26.87 -> next multiple of 5 is 30, plus 5 -> 35
#   runners_pins   29.83 30.13 30.36 -> worst 30.36 -> next multiple of 5 is 35, plus 5 -> 40
# The single 60s row becomes three rows summing to 120, so EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 1845 -> 1905.
# tests/test_go_toolchain.sh 45 -> 55 (change 0314): a file that GOT SLOWER, defended by measurement.
# Its uninstrumented `go test ./...` now compiles and runs change 0314's internal/process package,
# whose real-process launch/observe/stop/recover tests fork, exec, and wait on real children — real
# wall clock even uninstrumented, and no cost was avoidable to remove first: those tests ARE the
# change's acceptance proof. Re-measured standalone serial, one machine, as
# `scripts/run-tests.sh -j 1 --timings PATH tests/test_go_toolchain.sh` (a cluster of 45/45/45/46 with
# one loaded-machine reading at 48):
# The file now exceeds its old 45 row, so per this header's rule it is re-sized from the worst
# reading: next multiple of 5 above 48 is 50, plus the 5s margin -> 55, still well under the 60s
# ceiling. EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 2105 -> 2115.
# tests/test_go_finalize_e2e.sh is a NEW FILE brought by change 0316 (Task 17) — the header's
# new-test-file case. It runs the hermetic finalize end-to-end matrix
# (internal/app/finalize_e2e_test.go), which builds ./cmd/docket and a fake `gh` and drives full
# finalize lifecycles through CLI argv against real bare-remote repositories — genuine wall clock,
# and none avoidable: those lifecycles ARE the acceptance proof. It is deliberately NOT folded into
# tests/test_go_toolchain.sh's `go test ./...`: the matrix carries the `e2e` build tag, so the
# default-tag Go gate excludes it (it neither runs twice nor inflates that 55s row), and this file
# runs it alone behind `-tags e2e`. The build tag also lets the matrix use t.Parallel(), so the
# eight lifecycle tests overlap. Measured standalone serial, one machine, as
# `scripts/run-tests.sh -j 1 --timings PATH tests/test_go_finalize_e2e.sh`:
# Next multiple of 5 above 16 is 20, plus the 5s margin -> 25, well under the 60s ceiling.
# EXPECTED_TOTAL moves 2115 -> 2140.
